newsitem.title: ITALY: Jewish treasures held by Italy's Treasury - reports.
newsitem.headline: Jewish treasures held by Italy's Treasury - reports.

text.p: Gold, jewellery and other valuables stripped from Jews killed at a Nazi German death camp in northeast Italy in World War Two have been traced to a vault at the Italian Treasury, newspapers reported on Sunday.
The reports, which could not immediately be confirmed, said the valuables were contained in five crates which had been kept at the vault in central Rome since 1962.
The Corriere della Sera newspaper said the valuables had been traced to the vault by the prefect, or central government representative, in the northeast city of Trieste, Michele De Feis.
He launched an enquiry last year into the whereabouts of the missing treasure after Trieste's Jewish community raised a claim for compensation for victims of the Holocaust.
Trieste was under Nazi occupation from September 1943 until the end of the war in 1945. Many of the city's Jews perished at the nearby Risiera di San Sabba, the only Nazi death camp in Italy.
La Repubblica newspaper said the plundered treasure was moved to Klagenfurt in Austria by the retreating Germans in 1945 and returned to Trieste in the early 1950s.

"A commission was set up and a show (of the valuables) was organised but only a few of the items returned to their legitimate owners. Most of Trieste's Jews never returned from the camp," the newspaper said.
Neither De Feis nor Treasury officials could be contacted on Sunday about the reports.

The newspapers said Trieste's Jewish community raised the case after publicity about the controversy over whether Swiss banks kept millions of dollars deposited in secret accounts by Jews before and during the Second World War.
